title: Annual parades and the Mardi Gras ball on the wharf
summary: They discuss yearly holiday jobs and the white carnival ball played on the municipal wharf on Mardi Gras night.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I noticed here back, I guess it's about 19, 19 or 18, you had some funerals listed here. Different associations, looks like YNR Association Funeral, State Street. YMRA, I believe. And Young Men's Relief Association. Relief Association. That was one of the clubs at the society. Yeah, there was a society in the club too. For burial and all. I was wondering about your band, that was in 1920, these parades, I see. Every year you had the Emancipation Parade, you see, on the first of the years.
Carnival Parade, and the First of July, and everything. There was them holidays where the band would have jobs signed up for a year ahead, you know.
Yes, in February I noticed quite a few balls, and it says Carnival Ball.

Now that's the ball we used to play on the wharf after the night parade on the Mardi Gras night, you see. They played until twelve o'clock, and then they'd throw it down on the kind of length, sort of, at twelve o'clock that night. Yeah. But that was a ball that down me looked like. It used to take up a big space on the wharf. There wasn't no place around there to hold the people. It was a white ball, you see. And I'd need to charge the dollar to come in. And that would go to the Carnival Association for the expenses and things that you see around the city. Did you say that was down on the wharf? Oh, on the wharf. They put a campbells around a big place on the municipal wharf down there. Oh, yes. Right on the river. And then, man, it was down there so cold, man, it was almost freezing. Right there where the water would hit you, we would hit you right off the river. And we'd probably have that ball on every Mardi Gras, you see. Until yet they had a carnival ball down there, but the orchestra plays it now.
